The Francis-Henri Graffard-trained Drazinda has improved with each run this season after a nice debut win. After chasing down Victorious and Senorita Bonita in the Queen Mary when drawn on the wrong side, she placed second in a Listed race before going one better last month. A quality-looking edition of the Group 1 Prix Morny was a step too far, but this Sioux Nation filly still ran creditably and can continue her progression down in grade. metadata.summary: Lando Norris has revealed he had other opportunities before signing a new contract to stay at McLaren until at least the end of 2030.
metadata.content: Lando Norris reveals other 'opportunities' before signing new McLaren contract ahead of Italian Grand Prix | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Exclusive Lando Norris reveals other 'opportunities' before signing new McLaren contract ahead of Italian Grand Prix Sky Sports F1's Martin Brundle caught up with Lando Norris to discuss his new McLaren contract and the title race in an interview that will air this weekend; watch Friday's practice sessions for the Italian GP at 11.30am and 3pm, live on Sky Sports F1 Wednesday 2 September 2026 19:54, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch Lando Norris' roller-coaster season so far, which has seen several DNFs and race wins, putting him in the mix to challenge for the title Lando Norris has revealed he had other opportunities before signing a new contract to stay at McLaren until at least the end of 2030. Norris, who has won the last two Formula 1 races, has been with McLaren since making his F1 debut in 2019 and says the contract was "probably the easiest contract I've had to sign". The 26-year-old admitted though, in a wide-ranging interview with Sky Sports F1's Martin Brundle which will air at this weekend's Italian Grand Prix, that there were other options. metadata.summary: Claressa Shields has hailed the greatness of Katie Taylor and says she holds no qualms over a fight between the boxing greats never materialising.
metadata.content: Claressa Shields not upset Katie Taylor fight didn't happen and sends retirement message to Irish great | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to content Exclusive Claressa Shields not upset Katie Taylor fight didn't happen and sends retirement message to Irish great Claressa Shields and Amanda Serrano both wished Katie Taylor a happy retirement as the Irish great prepares for the final bout of her professional career this weekend; Shields played down the idea she was upset the two never shared the ring, praising Taylor's historic career. Stuart Hodge @Hodgeythehack Thursday 3 September 2026 06:25, UK Image: Katie Taylor closes the curtain on her historic career this weekend Claressa Shields has hailed the greatness of Katie Taylor and says she holds no qualms over a fight between the boxing greats never materialising. Taylor enters her farewell bout this weekend when she takes on Flora Pili in an undisputed super-lightweight world title clash at Dublin's Croke Park in front of more than 80,000 fans. The Irish icon, a two-weight undisputed world champion and Olympic gold medallist, will hang up her gloves widely-recognised as the greatest fighter in female boxing history. Five-weight world champion Shields has arguably become the closest rival to Taylor's reputation at the pinnacle of the sport. Taylor: I'm really retiring after Pili fight - I'm not like Fury! metadata.summary: Spanish wonderkid Rafael Jodar was involved in a testy exchange with a journalist following his stunning exit to Chinese lucky loser Bu Yunchaokete at the US Open on Wednesday.
metadata.content: US Open: Spanish wonderkid Rafael Jodar involved in testy exchange with journalist following shock exit at Flushing Meadows | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to content US Open: Spanish wonderkid Rafael Jodar involved in testy exchange with journalist following shock exit at Flushing Meadows Rafael Jodar was tripped up at the first hurdle of his maiden ‌US Open campaign before a heated exchanged with a journalist during his press conference; watch the US Open live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+, streaming service NOW and the Sky Sports app Thursday 3 September 2026 06:21, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at Rafael Jodar's frosty exchange after his shock defeat to Bu Yunchaokete at the US Open Spanish wonderkid Rafael Jodar was involved in a testy exchange with a journalist following his stunning exit to Chinese lucky loser Bu Yunchaokete at the US Open on Wednesday. Jodar was tripped up at the first hurdle of his maiden ‌campaign in New York, as the Spanish 12th seed failed to find his rhythm and fell 6-2 6-1 ‌6-1 to Bu. Back at the site of his junior triumph two ​years ago, 19-year-old Jodar looked unusually out of sorts after his first-round clash was delayed by a day due to ​rain, with a flurry of unforced errors in defeat.
